Follow-up to #305. CodeRabbit's review of 35b3536 left three non-blocking edge cases in `scripts/published-document-links.ts`. The audit should treat Markdown the way GitHub renders it: skip code spans and code blocks, read destinations with nested balanced parentheses, and handle a reference title that starts on the next line. Consider reusing a CommonMark-compliant parser rather than extending the hand-written matcher:

- [scripts/published-document-links.ts:44](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/pull/305#discussion_r4546020638): Exclude code text before checking destinations.
- [scripts/published-document-links.ts:48](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/pull/305#discussion_r4546020649): Read destinations with nested balanced parentheses.
- [scripts/published-document-links.ts:49](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/pull/305#discussion_r4546020658): Include a reference title that starts on the next line.

Each fix needs a test that fails on revert.

value.text: The Greptile env-PATH deferral is resolved in PR #305 round 6, matching the owner correction here. The nested test environment now prepends the actual Node executable directory to the explicit PATH without inheriting other PM variables. A real non-system Node fixture reproduces failure when only PATH forwarding is reverted, completes promptly with the fix, and passes with Node 22. Public CI evidence: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/actions/runs/43181118299/job/131057054329 . The Markdown follow-ups remain open and unchanged; this entry records only the resolved PATH portion.

### GitHub comments (3)

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-12T08:30:56Z)
>
> Also from #305 (Greptile on its round-5 head): [test/workspace-alias.test.ts:162](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/pull/305#discussion_r4547939159). The child test drops `PATH`, so its `#!/usr/bin/env node` fake CLI cannot find Node when Node is installed outside the system search path. Pass a safe search path that includes `path.dirname(process.execPath)`. Add a test with a non-system Node location that fails on revert.

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-12T08:52:33Z)
>
> Current hosted evidence corroborates the PATH follow-up above at PR #305 head `3d9f55110968a3194a44dea82bd40c1d6fba1639`: [Node 22 job 131057054329](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/actions/runs/43181118299/job/131057054329) completed 991 tests, 990 passed and 1 failed. The failing `workspace path assertions accept a symlinked temporary-directory prefix` child emits `env: 'node': No such file or directory` in the nested spawn-fallback test and then reaches the 60-second outer timeout. This is an observed CI-blocking test-environment failure, not evidence of a product authorization or serialization defect. The earlier captured-workspace identity check passes in this same log.
> 
> Acceptance remains the existing scoped fix: provide a safe child executable search path containing the directory of `process.execPath`, preserve environment isolation, and demonstrate the non-system Node regression test fails without that change and passes with it. Verify the nested process completes without waiting for the outer timeout. This adds hosted evidence to the existing owner rather than opening a duplicate.

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-12T11:26:04Z)
>
> Correction on the env-PATH point that #305 deferred here (Greptile, round 5): it was not cosmetic. With round 5 (3d9f551), CI fails on both Node versions inside the nested `node --test` run of `test/workspace-alias.test.ts` / `test/pm-runner.test.ts` ("spawn fallback stays non-blocking, serializes a workspace, and overlaps independent workspaces"). CodeRabbit then rated the same problem Major (#305 thread on `test/workspace-alias.test.ts:162`). It is back in scope for #305 round 6, so this issue no longer tracks that point. The other points here stay.
